snippet.title: Rupert And The Toymaker's Party (C64 Longplay)
snippet.description:
Published by Quicksilva in 1985 for £7.99.

Rupert is running late, so rather than taking the scenic route he chooses to make haste through the Toymaker's castle. Risking your life for a friend's party is dedication if nothing else. Rupert must navigate 7 levels, collecting all party invitations along the way, then locate the exit to the next castle area.

Collecting invitations whilst avoiding enemies requires precision, practice, and luck. Some screens include friendly magpies or planes that can be ridden; these are essential for reaching otherwise inaccessible areas.

The opening levels are straightforward enough, though things soon heat up. Difficulty curve is nicely pitched and strikes that delicate 'one more go' compulsion.

Graphics are pretty and lovely music. The title screen tune is quite melancholic just as I found Rupert Bear's theme, albeit a different tune.

Martin Walker was responsible for the coding, graphics, and music. I believe this was his first C64 venture. Martin was later responsible for games including Citadel and Hunter's Moon, and composed music for Armalyte, Speedball 2, SWIV, amongst many others. A talented chap indeed.
